summary: Propyl paraben is the propyl ester of para-hydroxybenzoic acid, used as an antimicrobial (mainly antifungal) preservative in pharmaceuticals, cosmetics and foods rather than as a therapeutic agent. It is added in low concentrations to prevent microbial spoilage of multidose formulations, often combined with methylparaben. It is generally well tolerated but can cause hypersensitivity/contact reactions in sensitized people (paraben allergy).
indications: Antimicrobial preservative to inhibit fungal and bacterial growth in oral, topical and parenteral pharmaceutical formulations
Preservative in cosmetics and as a food additive (where permitted)

moa: Parabens disrupt microbial membrane transport processes and inhibit synthesis of DNA, RNA and key enzymes in bacteria and fungi. Antimicrobial activity increases with alkyl chain length, so propyl paraben is more potent (especially against fungi) than methylparaben, while aqueous solubility decreases.

hepatic: Not relevant at the trace excipient concentrations used in formulations; parabens are hydrolyzed and conjugated, then renally excreted.

overdose: Overdose is not a clinical concern at excipient concentrations. Ingestion of large quantities of the pure substance could cause gastrointestinal irritation; manage symptomatically.
